display.purpose: Page-level hero heading. Rare — one per route at most.

headline.purpose: Route titles and major section openers.

title.purpose: The workhorse heading: card titles, panel headers, species names.

body.purpose: All running text. The global 16px/1.5 baseline.

label.purpose: Buttons, form labels, list metadata, input text at md+.

micro.purpose: Badges and dense map chrome. The floor — nothing smaller ships.

shadows.name: elevation-raised-subtle
shadows.purpose: Lightweight input chrome you look through rather than press — search field, select trigger. No hover escalation.

shadows.name: elevation-raised
shadows.purpose: Small static chrome above the map: cards, app sidebar, mobile nav bar.

shadows.name: elevation-raised-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover escalation for interactive raised surfaces, via .elevation-interactive.

shadows.name: elevation-floating
shadows.purpose: Dismiss-by-tap-outside surfaces: dropdown menus, select content, sheets, tooltips.

shadows.name: elevation-overlay
shadows.purpose: Blocking surfaces with a scrim: modal dialogs.

shadows.name: elevation-raised-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-theme raised. Same geometry as light; the 1px inset highlight is the real depth cue (ADR 0001).

shadows.name: button-lift
shadows.purpose: Resting lift on filled pill buttons — depth standing in for the border they don't have.

shadows.name: button-lift-hover
shadows.purpose: Button hover: the surface gets heavier, it never moves.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Canonical duration for default UI state changes.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The system's only easing curve. Every transition references it.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The go-signal: bright green fill, deep green label, borderless pill lifted by shadow.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; height: 2.75rem; padding: 0 1.5rem; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; font-family: 'Public Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--happy-500, oklch(0.74 0.17 150)); color: var(--happy-900, oklch(0.24 0.07 150)); box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.18); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.58 0.18 150); box-shadow: 0 3px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.22); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--happy-600, oklch(0.65 0.18 150)); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.18); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Danger without red: the deepest step of the green scale, white label. Severity is depth, not hue.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { background: var(--happy-900, oklch(0.24 0.07 150)); color: #fff; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.18); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: oklch(0.36 0.10 150); box-shadow: 0 3px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.22); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--happy-600, oklch(0.65 0.18 150)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The system's one sanctioned stroke: 2px green edge on transparent, readable-green label.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: var(--happy-700, oklch(0.42 0.13 150)); border: 2px solid var(--happy-600, oklch(0.65 0.18 150)); box-shadow: none; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--happy-50, oklch(0.97 0.03 152)); color: var(--happy-700, oklch(0.42 0.13 150)); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--happy-600, oklch(0.65 0.18 150)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Lowest-emphasis action: green label on nothing, washing to mist on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--happy-700, oklch(0.42 0.13 150)); box-shadow: none; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--happy-50, oklch(0.97 0.03 152)); color: var(--happy-700, oklch(0.42 0.13 150)); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--happy-600, oklch(0.65 0.18 150)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Search Field
components.description: 48px pill on warm paper with a raised-subtle lift; focus turns the border bright green. Leading-icon callers pad to 2.75rem.
components.css: .ds-field { position: relative; display: block; width: 100%; max-width: 22rem; } .ds-field-icon { position: absolute; left: 1rem; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); width: 1.125rem; height: 1.125rem; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.5261 0.0151 82.3829)); pointer-events: none; } .ds-input-search { display: flex; height: 3rem; width: 100%; padding: 0.25rem 1rem 0.25rem 2.75rem; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(0.9071 0.01 87.4748)); border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--card, oklch(0.9938 0.0013 106.4231)); color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.2431 0.0076 95.3724)); font-family: 'Public Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.06); outline: none; transition: color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-input-search::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.5261 0.0151 82.3829)); } .ds-input-search:focus-visible { border-color: var(--happy-500, oklch(0.74 0.17 150)); } .ds-input-search[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: var(--happy-900, oklch(0.24 0.07 150)); }

components.name: Badge
components.description: Borderless 12px pill marker. Default uses the literal bright green — one step brighter than --primary — so it reads as a marker, not a small button.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.25rem; width: fit-content; padding: 0.125rem 0.5rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--happy-500, oklch(0.74 0.17 150)); color: var(--happy-900, oklch(0.24 0.07 150)); font-family: 'Public Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.3; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; transition: color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-badge + .ds-badge { margin-left: 0.375rem; } .ds-badge-secondary { background: var(--secondary, oklch(0.9582 0.0193 147.8505)); color: var(--secondary-foreground, oklch(0.5262 0.1294 147.1971)); }

components.name: Trail Card
components.description: Photo-first container: 20px radius, no border, raised shadow that deepens on hover, media clipped full-bleed.
components.html:
Chanterelle

Cantharellus cibarius · Jul–Oct
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 1.25rem; overflow: hidden; background: var(--card, oklch(0.9938 0.0013 106.4231)); color: var(--card-foreground, oklch(0.2431 0.0076 95.3724)); box-shadow: 0 2px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); transition: box-shadow 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); max-width: 20rem; } .ds-card:hover { box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.14); } .ds-card-media { height: 8rem; background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--happy-300, oklch(0.85 0.12 151)), var(--happy-600, oklch(0.65 0.18 150))); } .ds-card-body { display: grid; gap: 0.375rem; padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem 1.5rem; } .ds-card-title { margin: 0; font-family: 'Space Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; } .ds-card-meta { margin: 0; font-family: 'Public Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.5261 0.0151 82.3829)); }

components.name: Nav Surface (glass)
components.description: The one nav treatment shared by desktop sidebar and mobile bottom bar: elevation raised plus glass-regular, with an opaque fallback and a green tint on the active item.
components.html: MapSpeciesRecipes
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: stretch; gap: 0.25rem; padding: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.3); border-top-color: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.5); border-radius: 1.25rem; background: var(--card, oklch(0.9938 0.0013 106.4231)); box-shadow: 0 2px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); width: fit-content; } @supports (backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) { .ds-nav { background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.9); backdrop-filter: blur(12px); } } @media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce), (prefers-contrast: more) { .ds-nav { background: var(--card, oklch(0.9938 0.0013 106.4231)); backdrop-filter: none; } } .ds-nav-item { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem; min-width: 4.5rem; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 0.75rem; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.2431 0.0076 95.3724)); font-family: 'Public Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-nav-item svg { width: 1.25rem; height: 1.25rem; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--happy-100, oklch(0.93 0.06 152)); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--happy-600, oklch(0.65 0.18 150)); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: var(--happy-100, oklch(0.93 0.06 152)); } .ds-nav-item-active svg { color: var(--happy-700, oklch(0.42 0.13 150)); }

narrative.overview:
The Trailhead is the moment before you set off: the signpost is green, the ground is warm, and everything you need to read is legible in full daylight. The map is the world — a living, unpredictable, edge-to-edge surface the interface has no control over — and every piece of chrome is something that floats above it: a signpost, a marker, a field card. The interface never competes with the terrain; it hovers over it and stays readable against whatever the terrain happens to be doing underneath.

The mood is fresh, alive, and tactile. A single spring-green hue does all the signalling, and it is a green with actual chroma in it — oklch(0.74 0.17 150), the color of new growth rather than corporate forest. Everything interactive is a soft-edged pill with a diffuse drop shadow and no border, so surfaces read as pressable objects sitting on warm paper rather than as boxes drawn onto a page. Warm neutrals carry the ground (#fdfdfc paper, #f1efe9 linen, #f2e8dc tan): there is no cool grey anywhere in the light theme, and the absence is deliberate — cool grey is what makes an outdoor tool feel like an admin panel.

Restraint is enforced in exactly one place and it is the sharpest rule in the system: there is no second hue. No red, not even for destructive actions. Severity is expressed as depth on the green scale, not as a change of hue. The one thing this system rejects is the multi-hue semantic palette — a green for success, a red for danger, a blue for info — and the rejection is already shipped in --destructive: var(--happy-900).
keyCharacteristics: One hue, seven steps: a spring-green scale carries brand, state, and severity alike.
Warm-neutral ground; zero cool grey in the light theme.
Five semantic elevation roles, chosen by meaning rather than by shadow value.
Glass as an opt-in material on small chrome only — never on the map, never on a dialog.
Contrast floors treated as hard limits, because the surface underneath is a photograph of the world.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: The Trailhead scale is the only brand hue on any screen. Severity is depth, not hue: --destructive resolves to --happy-900. The sole exception is safety warning amber, which exists because a toxic-lookalike warning must not read as decoration.

rules.name: The Text-Safe Step Rule
rules.body: Greens split into text-safe and fill-only. --happy-700 and Moss Text are text-safe. --happy-500 and the grass9-derived values are fills, rings, and non-text indicators only, held to the 3:1 non-text floor. Using a fill-only green as a text color is a contrast bug, not a style choice.

rules.name: The Light-Only Rule
rules.body: The --happy-* scale is a light-theme scale; it was never reviewed in dark mode. Dark-mode components fall back to the pre-existing tokens (Lichen, Night Surface) instead. When adding a component that hardcodes a --happy-* step, pair it with a dark-mode fallback that doesn't.

rules.name: The Warm Ground Rule
rules.body: No cool grey in the light theme. Every neutral carries a warm hue angle (64–107 in OKLCH). A #f5f5f5, a slate-100, or a pure #fff background is out of system.

rules.name: The Two-Family Rule
rules.body: h1–h3 are Space Grotesk automatically, via a global base rule. Everything else is Public Sans. Never set a display face on body copy, and never override a heading's family to match its surroundings.

rules.name: The German Test
rules.body: Every text container must survive its longest German string without clipping or reflowing its layout. Six locales ship; a label that only fits in English is broken. Test with de before considering a text-bearing component done.

rules.name: The Reserved Faces Rule
rules.body: Merriweather and Source Code Pro are declared but unused. Introducing either is a design decision that needs a reason — long-form reading matter for the serif, data or coordinates for the mono — not a default reach for variety.

rules.name: The Fixed Shell Rule
rules.body: The app shell never scrolls. If content overflows, it gets its own scroll container; adding scroll to body breaks the map canvas.

rules.name: The Role-Not-Value Rule
rules.body: Apply .elevation-raised, not a shadow-[…] arbitrary value. A hand-rolled shadow on a new component is drift, and it will not track the dark-theme inset highlight.

rules.name: The Base-Has-No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: The map canvas is base: no class, no shadow, no glass. It is not a discrete surface and deliberately has no utility to reach for.

rules.name: The Glass Scope Rule
rules.body: Glass goes only on small, fixed-size, non-text-heavy raised or floating chrome. Never on base (the map), never on overlay (dialogs are text-heavy and contrast-critical over an unpredictable background), and never on anything that animates its own size.

rules.name: The Opaque-First Rule
rules.body: Every glass surface defines its opaque background first and layers translucency on top inside @supports (backdrop-filter: blur(1px)). prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce and prefers-contrast: more both drop back to opaque. An unsupporting browser must never render near-invisible chrome over a photograph.

rules.name: The Pill-Or-Card Rule
rules.body: Interactive and small → fully round. Container → 20px. There is no middle radius for a component to invent; if a new surface is neither, decide which of the two it is behaving as.

rules.name: The Borderless Default Rule
rules.body: New components get no border. Separation comes from elevation and background contrast. The outline button pair is the sanctioned exception, and it stays a pair.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Movement Rule
rules.body: Interaction feedback changes shadow and background. It does not scale, translate, or rotate chrome. The one sanctioned transform is the mobile nav's active-item scale.

dos: Do pick an elevation role (.elevation-raised, .elevation-floating) and let the shadow follow. Reach for .elevation-interactive when the surface responds to hover.
Do keep every green in its lane: --happy-700 and Moss Text for text and icons, --happy-500 for fills and indicators only.
Do express severity as depth on the green scale. --destructive is --happy-900 and that is correct, not a placeholder.
Do define the opaque background before the translucent one on any glass surface, and honor prefers-reduced-transparency and prefers-contrast.
Do consume NAV_SURFACE_CLASS for any new nav chrome instead of respelling elevation-raised glass-regular.
Do keep interactive targets at 44px or larger (48px for the search field). Field use with cold hands is a real constraint.
Do add tokens to the @theme block in src/index.css — that is the live theme.
Do pair any component that hardcodes a --happy-* step with a dark-mode fallback on the pre-Trailhead tokens.
Do test text-bearing components in German before calling them done.
donts: Don't introduce a second hue. No red for destructive, no blue for info, no amber outside genuine foraging safety warnings.
Don't write an arbitrary shadow-[…] on a new component. It bypasses the role system and will not pick up the dark-theme inset highlight.
Don't treat --shadow-* as the elevation scale. It is legacy, materially weaker than what ships, and aliasing to it regresses the live look (ADR 0001).
Don't put glass on the map canvas, on a dialog, or on anything text-heavy or size-animating.
Don't use --happy-500 or any grass9-derived green as a text color. It is held to the 3:1 non-text floor only.
Don't use --happy-700 for the mobile nav's active tint — 1.7:1 over translucent dark chrome on a light map.
Don't add a cool grey or a pure #ffffff to the light theme. Every neutral is warm.
Don't add a border to a new primitive. The outline button pair (outline, enhanced-outline) is the system's entire bordered vocabulary.
Don't put theme values in tailwind.config.js — it carries no theme and is retained only for the shadcn CLI.
Don't make body scroll. The shell is fixed at 100dvh; give overflowing content its own scroll container.
Don't apply a surface treatment to the Sidebar's positioning container. It must land on data-slot='sidebar-inner' or the background paints over it.
